# read_C: pp. 87–89 (leaves n88–n90), plus the first two lines of p. 90 (n91), read from the images

## Lines and where things start and end

- p. 87 (n88) has five lines. It is a leaf front and opens with `༄༅༔` followed by a wide blank, then `༔`.
- p. 88 (n89) has five lines. It is a leaf back and has no ornament.
- p. 89 (n90) has five lines. It is a leaf front and opens `༄༅༔ ༔`. Line 89.1 is short: it ends at x≈1650 with `…ཐབས་མེད་དོ༔`, and an empty framed box fills the rest of the line.
- p. 90 (n91) is a leaf back. I read only its lines 1–2.
- **Ornament form.** On both n88 and n90 the opening ornament is a horizontal swirl, with a tail at the left and two curls. It is not the stacked ༄༅ of the kha leaves.
  - Reader A wrote this shape as ࿐ (pp. 82–83). Reader B wrote ༄༅ (p. 85).
  - I wrote `༄༅༔ ༔` to match B and part 008. The shape matches A's description, so the readers should settle on one form. If it is ࿐, change 87.1 and 89.1 to `࿐༔ ༔`.
- In all: 15 print lines on my pages, plus 2 lines of p. 90.

**Where my part starts.** p. 87 starts at the witness's `…ནང་ནས་གསང་སྔགས་ཀྱི་ཉམས་ལེན་མེད་པས༔`.
- The print's first syllable after the ornament is `སྔགས`.
- So p. 86 must end with `…གསང་` (or similar). Reader B should check this.

**Where the part ends.** No sentence closes near the end of p. 89.
- p. 89 ends mid-sentence: `…ཐོས་གྲོལ་ཆེན་མོ་འདི་ནི་མ་བསྒོམ་པར` | p. 90 `སངས་རྒྱས་པའི་ཆོས༔`.
- After that comes a list of `…ཆོས༔` items, then `…ཆོས་ཟབ་མོ་ཡིན་ཏེ༔`. Neither closes a sentence.
- The first sentence end is **p. 90 line 2, `…ངན་སོང་དུ་སོང་བ་མི་སྲིད་དོ༔`** at x≈1690. The part ends there, and the next part begins with `འདི་དང` (the last word of 90.2).

There is one fallback. If the editor prefers to end on p. 89, the last sentence end on that page is in 89.4 (x≈1150): `…ངོས་ཟིན་ནས་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུ་ཐོབ་བོ༔`. That would leave about 1.5 lines of p. 89 for the next part.

**Proposed `# name:`** `The bardo of the wrathful deities begins`. An alternative is `Why the wrathful bardo is hard, and what hearing does`.
- From the witness, pp. 81–89 hold: the start of the wrathful-deities bardo; the 58 blood-drinkers who come; why recognising them is hard but freeing; the monastic scholar and the lax mantrin; the signs at death; and the worth of this text.
- No wrathful deity is described on pp. 87–89. Buddha Heruka (day 8) starts after p. 90 (witness: `…ད་ནི་ཞག་བརྒྱད་པ་ལ…`). So "first wrathful deities" does not fit these pages, unless pp. 81–86 already describe one, which the witness does not.

## Method

- **Line bands** came from row profiles. Headlines were at about:
  - n88: 120, 175, 235, 290, 350
  - n89: 140, 195, 250, 305, 360
  - n90: 135, 195, 250, 305, 360
- **Line slope** is small (about +0.02 px/px on n88, −0.02 px/px on n89).
- **Crops** were taken at ×2.5–×3 in three or four overlapping segments per line. Doubtful syllables were crops at ×4–×10 (LANCZOS/BICUBIC), with threshold-128 pixel dumps for line ends, tshegs and letter shapes.
- **Tshegs inside lines.** This print's mid-line tshegs are mostly fused to the head bars. Where the image cannot decide, I followed the witness's tsheg, as read_A did.
- **Line-end tshegs** were all checked by pixel dump.

## Where the other recension differs in sense (print followed)

- **87.4:** print `མོས་པ་བྱས་པ་ཙམ་ཀྱང` ("merely having faith"), other recension `བྱས་པ་ཁོ་ན་ཀྱང` ("by faith alone"). The sense is close.
- **87.5:** print `འཆི་བའི་ཚེ་ན` ("at the time of dying"), other recension `ཤི་བའི་ཚེ` ("when dead"). The sense is close.
- **88.1:** print `འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་ཏེ༔ དེས་ན་…ཕྱིར་རོ༔`. The clause chain links on to the next sentence, where the other recension closes with `འགྱུར་རོ༔`.
- **88.5:** the print adds `བྱོན་པ`: "the appearing of relics … is the sign of it".
- **88.5:** print `མཚན་ཉིད་པ` ("dialecticians"), other recension `མཚན་ཉིད་སྟོན་པ` ("teachers of dialectics").
- **89.2:** print "the great meditators who **cultivate** Dzogchen and Mahāmudrā" (`རྫོགས་ཆེན་པ་དང་ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོ་ལ་སོགས་པ་བསྒོམ་པའི`). The other recension phrases the same idea differently. The sense is the same.
- **89.3:** print `ཐོས་གྲོལ་འདི་` without `ཆེན་མོ`, and `ཀློག` (to read) for `ཀླག`. Same.
- **89.4–5:** print `…སྤྲུལ་སྐུ་ཐོབ་པ་དང༔ གཞན་དག་ཀ[?]ས[?] མཐོ་རིས་སུ་སྐྱེ་བ་སྟེ` ("…obtain the emanation body, and others [too?] are born in the higher realms"). Other recension: `སྤྲུལ་སྐུ་ཐོབ་པ་དང་གནས་མཐོ་རུས་སུ་སྐྱེས་ཏེ` ("obtain the emanation body and are born in a high state/family"). **The print adds a second group of people.**
- **89.5:** print `སྐྱེ་བ་ཕྱི་མ་ཆགས[?]་ལ་སྤྱོད་པའི་ལས་འཕྲོ`, other recension `སྐྱེ་བ་ཕྱི་མ་ལ་སྤྱོད་པའི་ལས་འཕྲོ`. The extra `ཆགས` is unclear in sense.
- **90.1:** print `སྡིག་པོ་ཆེ་གསང་ལམ་ལ་འཁྲིད་པ` ("leads great sinners onto the **secret** path"), other recension `ཆེ་གསེབ་ལམ་ལ` ("onto the path from among the …"). **This is a sense difference.**
- **90.2:** print `ངན་སོང་དུ་སོང་བ་མི་སྲིད` ("cannot have gone to the lower realms"), other recension `འགྲོ་བ` ("cannot go"). The sense is close.


Notes on the fixes:
- 88.2 `དགོྶ`: the line-end subscript-ས abbreviation (×8: a ས hook under གོ). It also lacks the join tsheg.
- 88.3/88.4 `རྟག`|`སུ`: read as the print's shared-ས contraction across the line break (the ག is squeezed against the frame and no ས follows it). If the editor reads the ས as simply dropped, the same fix applies.
- 88.4→88.5 (`…[…]ད་` | `ང༔`): depends on how the gap is resolved. If it is `[ཟེར]་དང༔`, the stray blob after ད should be dropped (`ད་ང༔ => དང༔`).
- 89.4→89.5 `ཀས`|`མཐོ`: wait until the `ཀ[?]ས[?]` reading is settled. It will probably need `…[?]་མཐོ`.
- No `པའཾ` / `ལཾ` / `ནམཁའ` forms occur. Both instances of `ནམ་མཁ…` are written in full.

## Suspected misprints

1. **88.4 `ནམ་མཁར་ལ`** for `ནམ་མཁའ་ལ` ("in the sky"). The letter is clearly ར (montage against the འ of `མཁའ` earlier in the same line). The sense allows only མཁའ. Moderate to high certainty. Proposed: `# fix: ནམ་མཁར་ལ་རོལ => ནམ་མཁའ་ལ་རོལ`.
2. **88.4 `རོལ་མོར་སྒྲ`** for `རོལ་མོའི་སྒྲ` ("sound of music"). Same letter shape. Probably the same confusion (ར for འ, with the gi-gu missing). Moderate certainty. Proposed: `# fix: རོལ་མོར་སྒྲ => རོལ་མོའི་སྒྲ`. If the editor prefers caution: kept, note only.
3. **87.1 `ཤི་རམ`** for `ཤ་རི་རམ` (śarīram, relic pellets). This is probably the print's own loan-word spelling. Kept, note only.
4. **88.2 `སོགས་པ་ཉམས་སུ`** (other recension `སོགས་པས`): the ས after པ is missing, but the sense survives. Kept, note only.
5. **88.3 `རྟག|སུ`**: see the fixes. It is either a contraction or a dropped ས.

## Open

- The two gaps (88.4 end, 89.3 end) and 89.4 `ཀ[?]ས[?]` need a second look, ideally on a better scan (archive.org n89/n90 at w3000).
- The p. 86 / p. 87 seam: read_B's p. 86 ends `…ནང་ནས་གསང་` with a tsheg, and my p. 87 begins `[ornament]༔ ༔སྔགས་ཀྱི`. That gives `གསང་སྔགས`, so the seam is clean.
